claim_boundary: fresh rendered Brain Workshop evidence tests an isolated opaque probe-profile utility memory; no controller learning, no replay, and no n-back mastery claim

comparison.interpretation: Conditioning utility on an opaque model probe profile preserved the established causal signal but did not improve target recovery; confidence gating prevented sparse utility evidence from displacing the baseline selector while adding 30 verifier bits, 15 logical lifetimes, and 15 consumed probe rows.

controls.long_horizon_arm: not promoted separately; active two-step remained 0/3 versus 1/3 passive

interpretation: The profile-conditioned memory is a cleaner reusable boundary than global intention utility, but it is not a measured capability gain at this exposure. The remaining bottleneck is utility transfer across sufficiently repeated uncertainty contexts: one outcome per candidate is too sparse to learn a reliable policy, and profile matching alone does not yet create that evidence.
